text:
alex: quick check — i've got a small NUMA-aware prefetch prototype that tries to demote cold GPU pages to host and prefetch hot ranges back based on upcoming token windows. want opinions on the interface boundary between 'placement' and 'admission'

mira: nice. can you sketch the API you're thinking of?

alex: sure. current idea: `prefetch_hint(tenant, vec<page_ranges>, priority, deadline_ms)` and a separate `placement_decision(page_id)` sync query used by the runtime when scheduling eviction. simple for now.

samir: two immediate flags: 1) who controls backpressure? admission should be able to reject prefetches under high IO/latency. 2) we need tenant fairness so a noisy tenant can't flood host staging.

ingrid: +1 on admission control. also prefer async callback rather than blocking `placement_decision`, so callers can continue and react to a decision event.

taylor: curious about heuristics — are you using token-window lookahead from the scheduler or model-level signals?

alex: prototype pulls lookahead from scheduler (sequence length + context offsets) + cheap LRU hot-score. combining both gives ~20% fewer roundtrips in local testing.

samir: payload shape question: page_ranges is ok but what about meta like `expected_residency_ms` and `recompute_cost_est`? would help admission prioritization.

alex: added `expected_residency_ms` in my branch. recompute_cost is tougher but we could plumb an enum: {cheap, medium, expensive}.

ingrid: we should define a clear fallback policy: if prefetch fails, runtime should be able to issue a low-latency on-demand load path (no long stalls). that implies different QoS for prefetch vs sync load.

optimizer-bot: perf-note: recent test on rtxp4-32 shows async prefetch + cheap recompute reduces median p99 by ~60ms for short chats (internal run id 2026-03-18-67).

taylor: nice. long-term thought: this feels like it belongs to a 'placement orchestrator' microcomponent that only exposes high-level intents (hot/cold/demote) and a separate 'admission' controller that enforces capacity & debt across tenants. would help when we add remote NVMe tier later.

samir: agree. separation will let us swap admission policies (token-bucket, epoch quotas) without changing placement heuristics. also makes testing easier.

alex: i worry about cross-module latency if we make decisions too chatty. we should define a compact binary wire (or shared ring) for intents+ack to keep per-alloc cost O(1).

ingrid: +1. also add telemetry hooks: prefetch_issued, prefetch_accepted, prefetch_failed (reason), prefetch_latency, and per-tenant rejected_count.

taylor: small nit: catalog the transitions clearly: GPU-resident -> demoted-host-staging -> remote-cold. each transition should have a single source-of-truth for policy. duplicates cause bugs.

alex: noted. i'll draft an RFC that: 1) defines the prefetch/admission APIs, 2) proposes the placement/admission split, 3) lists telemetry and fallback policies, and 4) shows a tiny perf experiment.

samir: please include a simple admissions POC: `admit_prefetch(tenant, bytes)` returning {admitted:bool, delay_ms}, so we can experiment with burst smoothing.

alex: will do. aim to post RFC by EOD tomorrow. thanks for the quick feedback :thumbsup:

mira: thanks — if you want i can pair on the perf experiment tomorrow morning.

alex: yes please, appreciate it.

optimizer-bot: reminder: add feature-flag gate `numa_prefetch_v1` and a metrics flag for histograms.

alex: done, adding flags to the draft.
